description:
Redwood Inference will publish a public-facing benchmark report focused on production inference economics: latency and cost efficiency (latency/$) across a curated set of LLMs and deployment regions. The project pairs a rigorous, reproducible benchmarking methodology (owned by Applied ML + Runtime + Infra) with a coordinated go-to-market launch (owned by Marketing + Product Marketing + Sales Enablement), designed to drive top-of-funnel developer signups and sales-assisted pipeline for Dedicated and Private.

Goals:
- Publish a credible, technically defensible benchmark report comparing model+region performance on Redwood (and, where appropriate, contextual competitor baselines with clear caveats).
- Ship an interactive web experience (tables/filters) + downloadable PDF report + blog post.
- Enable Sales/SE/CS with talk tracks, FAQs, objection handling, and a packaged “how we measured” explainer.
- Run a coordinated launch: email, community, social, partner channels, analyst briefings, and a webinar.
- Instrument results and measure impact: traffic, signups, activation, demo requests, SQLs, influenced pipeline, and brand lift.

Scope (in-scope):
- Benchmark design: workload definitions (prefill/decode mix), prompt sets, concurrency levels, token sizes, warmup, caching policy, and stability checks.
- Data collection across regions (NA/EU/APAC where available), normalization to a single “latency/$” metric with supporting metrics (p50/p95, throughput, $/1M tokens).
- Reproducibility artifacts: code, configs, run manifests, data validation, and review/approval workflow.
- Content production: report narrative, methodology section, charts, landing page copy, and press kit.
- Launch operations: editorial calendar, stakeholder reviews (Product, Legal, Security), sales enablement distribution, and post-launch follow-up.

Out-of-scope (explicit):
- Long-running ongoing benchmark program (beyond a short post-launch maintenance window).
- Building new product features solely for benchmark optics (only small guardrail/telemetry changes allowed).

Key stakeholders:
- Executive sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO), Camila Reyes (VP Marketing)
- PMM/Launch lead: Soojin Lee (Director of Product Marketing)
- Content lead: Ethan Wallace (Content Marketing)
- Benchmark technical leads: Jonas Weber (Dir Performance & Evals), Claire Dubois (Sr Research Engineer), Rina Kobayashi (Perf Benchmarks)
- Infra/Runtime partners: Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng Runtime), Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet), Neha Kapoor/Sean Gallagher (Reliability)
- Product input: Henry Cho (PM benchmarks/performance transparency), Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API)
- DevEx/docs: Elliot Price, Wei Chen, Renee Sullivan
- Sales enablement/users: Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer, AEs/SDR, Markus Klein (Solutions)
- Legal/compliance review: Michael Grant, Sofia Mendes (claims/terms)

Timeline (example, ~8 weeks):
- Weeks 1–2: methodology lock + instrumentation + draft outline; define model list and regions; create review checklist.
- Weeks 3–5: run benchmark sweeps; validate data; draft report copy; design landing page and charts.
- Weeks 6–7: internal reviews (Eng/PM/Sales/Legal), finalize web + PDF; create enablement kit; pre-brief analysts/partners.
- Week 8: launch week execution + live monitoring + post-launch debrief and iteration plan.

Constraints/risks:
- Methodology credibility (avoid cherry-picking; publish caveats, configs, and confidence/stability notes).
- Region capacity variability (need capacity reservations and repeat runs).
- Legal risk around comparative claims (clear language, source-of-truth data retention).
- Sales messaging consistency (single talk track + FAQ to avoid overclaiming).
